text:
Mike: Heads-up — ran the A/B for v2.4 (int8 hybrid) across splitwise slices, small lift on relevance but noticed tail latency drift. sharing quick numbers from eval-bot.
Ari: link to evals? :eyes:
Mike: eval-bot posted summary — see below. overall MRR +0.6% (95% CI +0.2, +1.0) but p99 latency +120ms and p999 spikes on longdoc slices.
Lina: can you paste the slice breakdown? wondering if it's one cohort blowing up.
Mike: copy/paste from eval-bot:

```
Sliced metrics (v2.4 vs baseline):
- short Q&A: MRR +0.9% | p99 +15ms
- multi-turn support: MRR +0.4% | p99 +70ms
- longdoc/summary: MRR -0.2% | p99 +340ms | p999 +820ms
- safety-heavy: neutral
- error-rate delta: +0.005 (ppm)
```

Ari: that longdoc p999 is the problem. user impact probably small overall but tail could hit SLA for a few customers.
Sam: Did we see increased CPU/GPU queueing or cache churn on those requests? Maybe kv-cache eviction on long contexts.
Eva: checked infra graphs: GPU utilization steady, but host-side preproc latency spikes aligned with longdoc requests. also a higher number of token expansions per request.
Lina: sounds like a warm-up/kv-warmth mismatch. If the model uses a different chunking pattern, cache hit-rate drops -> more memory ops.
Mike: agreed. Proposal: add an adaptive rollback trigger that looks at a composite signal (p99 delta and MRR delta) per slice rather than global.
Ari: sketch what that rule looks like.
Mike: proposal snippet:

```
rollback_rules:
  - name: longdoc_tail_protect
    slices: ["longdoc-summaries", "longdoc-extract"]
    conditions:
      - metric: p999_latency_ms
        threshold_delta: 500    # absolute ms
      - metric: mrr_pct_delta
        threshold_delta: -0.5   # percent points
    action: immediate-fallback
    cooloff: 10m
  - name: global_safety
    conditions:
      - metric: p99_latency_ms
        relative_threshold_pct: 30
      - metric: error_rate_ppm
        absolute_threshold: 100
    action: staged-decrement
```

Sam: I like per-slice rollbacks. We should also stage a throttled traffic cut (e.g., reduce split weight by 50% when p99>threshold) before full fallback.
Eva: can we automate sample extraction so we can repro the longdoc failures quickly? ops can hook dump artifacts when rule fires.
Lina: yes, add 'capture_sample: true' to action payload.
Ari: What about hysteresis? Last time we saw oscillations when we toggled quickly.
Mike: include a half-life window + require sustained violation for 5m before immediate-fallback, or use staged-decrement first. rule defined above had cooloff but we need ramp thresholds.
Sam: operational checklist:
- add rule to gating config repo
- run synthetic load targeted at longdoc slices in staging with same token expansion distribution
- enable sample capture and attach runbook link
- deploy a staged throttle (50% weight) as intermediate action

Eva: I'll add a quick dashboard with slice-level p50/p95/p99/p999 and mrr_delta. deploy-bot can wire alerts to #incidents if p999 > 700ms on longdoc.
deploy-bot: scheduled job created: canary-slice-dashboard -> alert rule set -> pager off by default
Lina: one more ask — can we add quantization diagnostic logs to help correlate kernel fallback events? maybe the runtime fell back to slower kernels on certain attention patterns.
Mike: good point. add runtime flag to log kernel choices for sampled requests.
Ari: timeline? if we can stage tests today we can promote rule to prod tomorrow for a low-traffic rollout.
Mike: I'll PR the gating rule and the dashboard. PR link when ready.
Eva: thanks — useful plan. :thumbsup:
Ari: will monitor the staging run.
Lina: ping me on PR review, I’ll check the diag logs.
Mike: cheers everyone, will follow-up with PR and the synthetic test results.
